mainTopic: Moving a ladder to a dovecote on יום טוב, רבי חייא's sons' mistaken rulings, and whether בית שמאי and בית הלל are consistent about שמחת יום טוב
overview: The גמרא notes that our משנה does not follow a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. In that ברייתא, בית שמאי and בית הלל both allow carrying a ladder from one dovecote to another, and they argue only about bringing it back. רבי יהודה adds that this applies only to a dovecote ladder: an attic ladder is forbidden by everyone. רבי דוסא allows only tilting the ladder from window to window. Then the גמרא tells how רבי חייא's sons permitted an attic ladder (or, in another version, tilting an attic ladder) and their father made them reverse it. In both versions their mistake was reading a later sage as more lenient than the תנא קמא, when he was really explaining him or being stricter. The גמרא then learns from our משנה that on שמחת יום טוב, בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient. It contrasts this with the משנה about covering blood, where the roles look reversed, and brings רבי יוחנן's answer that the names there are switched. It then moves the whole question to the משנה about taking young doves, and the challenge to רבי יוחנן's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says our משנה disagrees with a ברייתא. In the ברייתא, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says both בית שמאי and בית הלל allow carrying a ladder between dovecotes, and they argue only about bringing it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not match this תנא. A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that you may carry the ladder from one dovecote to another. They argue only about returning it. בית שמאי say you may not return it, and בית הלל say you may even return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a ברייתא tells the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל differently from our משנה, and it quotes that ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, בית שמאי forbid carrying the ladder from dovecote to dovecote, and only בית הלל allow it. In רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version, carrying it there is allowed by everyone. The argument moves to a later stage: may you bring the ladder back afterward?

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Does not follow this sage's opinion
Ladder
Dovecote (a house for pigeons or doves)
They agree
To return it (to its original place)

steps.confusionAlert: In this ברייתא, בית הלל's words 'אף מחזירין' mean 'you may EVEN bring it back.' Carrying it to the second dovecote is already allowed by everyone. Do not mix this version up with the version in our משנה.

phrases.english: Our mishnah is not in accordance with this tanna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:
Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel agree
that one may carry the ladder from one dovecote to another.
phrases.notes: The ladder is used to reach the doves to take them for food on יום טוב.

phrases.english: They disagree only about returning it,
as Beit Shammai say: One may not return it,
and Beit Hillel say: One may even return it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the משנה (from earlier in the daf) by bringing a ברייתא that tells the dispute differently.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, everyone allows carrying the ladder between dovecotes. בית שמאי forbid returning it, and בית הלל allow even that.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: this applies only to a dovecote ladder, not an attic ladder
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה limits the permission to a ladder made for a dovecote. Moving an attic ladder is forbidden by everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When does this apply? To a dovecote ladder. But with an attic ladder, everyone agrees it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a limit: the permission to move the ladder is only for a ladder that obviously belongs to a dovecote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone can tell that a dovecote ladder is being used for the doves. An attic ladder has many uses, so people seeing it carried might think you are going to fix your roof, which is real work. Because of that worry about how it looks (מראית עין), both בית שמאי and בית הלל forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (a phrase that introduces a limit)
An attic ladder (a general-use house ladder)
Everyone agrees
Forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the center of the first version of the story that follows, where רבי חייא's sons misread it. In the second version (איכא דאמרי), their mistake is about רבי דוסא instead.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים —
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: In what case is this said?
With regard to a dovecote ladder,
but with regard to an attic ladder,
everyone agrees it is prohibited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא by setting limits on the ladder case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Moving an attic ladder is forbidden according to both בית שמאי and בית הלל.

steps.title: רבי דוסא and אחרים: smaller ways of moving the ladder
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא allows tilting the ladder from window to window. אחרים, quoting him, also allow 'walking' the ladder by shifting its legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says: You may tilt it from one window to another. אחרים say in the name of רבי דוסא: You may even shift it along by moving its legs.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with smaller, more limited ways of moving the ladder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tilting the ladder inside the same dovecote is a very small movement, so it is allowed. As step 10 explains, רבי דוסא is actually stricter than the תנא קמא: even a dovecote ladder may only be tilted, not carried. אחרים, in his name, also allow moving it by shuffling its legs, which is still not fully carrying it.

keyTerms.meaning: He tilts it
From window to window (openings of the same dovecote)
'Others', an unnamed group of sages
Move it step by step by shifting its legs

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר: מַטֵּהוּ מֵחַלּוֹן לְחַלּוֹן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says: One may tilt it from window to window.
Aḥerim say in the name of Rabbi Dosa:
One may even shift it along by its legs.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר: מַטֵּהוּ מֵחַלּוֹן לְחַלּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with more opinions about how the ladder may be moved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tilting the ladder from window to window is allowed. According to אחרים, shifting it along by its legs is also allowed.

steps.title: רבי חייא's sons permit a ladder, and their father reverses it
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא's sons came back from the villages and said they had permitted moving a ladder. Their father told them to go back and forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons of רבי חייא went out to the villages. When they came back, their father asked them: Did any case come before you? They said: A ladder case came before us, and we permitted it. He said to them: Go out and forbid what you permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about this law. רבי חייא's sons permitted an attic ladder, and he ordered them to undo their ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ladder in the story was an attic ladder, and they permitted it. רבי חייא held that an attic ladder is forbidden by everyone, as רבי יהודה said. The story sets up the next question: why did the sons think it was allowed?

keyTerms.meaning: Villages
A real case that needed a halachic ruling
We permitted it
Forbid!

phrases.english: The sons of Rabbi Ḥiyya went out to the villages.
When they came back, their father said to them:
Did any case come before you?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: סוּלָּם בָּא לְיָדֵינוּ, וְהִתַּרְנוּהוּ.
phrases.english: They said to him: A ladder came before us, and we permitted it.
phrases.notes: This was an attic ladder being moved to a dovecote.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: צְאוּ וְאִסְרוּ מַה שֶּׁהִתַּרְתֶּם.
phrases.english: He said to them: Go out and prohibit what you permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a real case in which רבי יהודה's limit was applied.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Moving an attic ladder on יום טוב is forbidden, and a ruling that permitted it must be reversed.

steps.title: Why the sons thought it was allowed
steps.stepSummary: The sons reasoned like this: רבי יהודה said there is no argument about an attic ladder, so the תנא קמא must hold that there IS an argument, with בית הלל permitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought: Since רבי יהודה said they do not argue about an attic ladder, that shows the תנא קמא holds that they do argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the sons' reasoning. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons read רבי יהודה's words as disagreeing with the תנא קמא. If רבי יהודה needed to say 'everyone forbids an attic ladder,' they figured, then the תנא קמא must have included attic ladders in the dispute. That would mean בית הלל permit it, so the sons ruled like the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: They thought
By inference; this implies
The first sage quoted in the ברייתא
They disagree

phrases.aramaic: אִינְהוּ סְבוּר: מִדְּקָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: They thought: From the fact that Rabbi Yehuda said
that with regard to an attic ladder they do not disagree,
this implies that the first tanna holds that they do disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the sons' mistaken ruling in the story.
steps.raayaObject: That according to the תנא קמא, בית הלל permit moving even an attic ladder.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from רבי יהודה's words 'everyone agrees it is forbidden,' read as an argument against the תנא קמא.

steps.title: The real reading: רבי יהודה explains the first opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the sons' reasoning. רבי יהודה is not arguing with the תנא קמא; he is explaining what the תנא קמא meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. רבי יהודה is explaining the reason of the תנא קמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the sons' reasoning was wrong and gives the correct way to read רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons treated רבי יהודה as disagreeing with the תנא קמא. In fact, the תנא קמא was talking only about a dovecote ladder, and רבי יהודה just spells that out. So no one permits an attic ladder, and רבי חייא was right to reverse the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so
His reason
Is explaining

steps.whatToRemember: Moving an attic ladder is forbidden by everyone. רבי יהודה explains the תנא קמא; he does not argue with him. Not every added statement in a ברייתא is a disagreement.
steps.confusionAlert: When a later sage adds 'everyone agrees' (דברי הכל), it does not always mean he disagrees with the first opinion. Here he is only explaining it.

phrases.english: But that is not so;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה טַעְמֵיהּ דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא קָא מְפָרֵשׁ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda is explaining the reason of the first tanna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference the sons drew in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the sons' whole reading that the תנא קמא lets בית הלל permit an attic ladder.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They read an explanation as a disagreement. רבי יהודה only clarifies the תנא קמא's case and reason.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Everyone forbids moving an attic ladder on יום טוב, which is why רבי חייא reversed his sons' ruling.

steps.title: Proof from the words 'from dovecote to dovecote'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that the תנא קמא is only talking about a dovecote ladder, so רבי יהודה is just explaining him.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know? Because the ברייתא says: 'One may carry the ladder from dovecote to dovecote.' If the argument were about an attic ladder, it should have said 'carry the ladder TO a dovecote.' So it must mean: a dovecote ladder, yes; an attic ladder, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its rejection from Step 6 by bringing proof from the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An attic ladder normally stands by the house, so moving it would mean bringing it TO the dovecote. The words 'from dovecote to dovecote' show that the ladder already lives at the dovecotes. So the תנא קמא only permits a dovecote ladder, which is exactly what רבי יהודה said.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?
If it enters your mind (a suggestion the גמרא will reject)
It should have said
Dovecote (a structure where doves are raised)
Attic ladder, a regular household ladder

phrases.english: From where do we know? From the fact that it teaches:
One may carry the ladder from dovecote to dovecote
And if it enters your mind
that they argue about an attic ladder
then this phrase, 'one may carry the ladder from dovecote to dovecote'
should instead have said 'one may carry the ladder to a dovecote'
phrases.notes: Meaning: from the house to the dovecote.

phrases.english: Rather, is this not what it is saying:
a dovecote ladder: yes, permitted
an attic ladder: no, not permitted

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies textual proof for the rejection in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the תנא קמא only permits a dovecote ladder, so רבי יהודה is explaining and not arguing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording 'מוליכין את הסולם משובך לשובך' instead of 'לשובך'.

steps.title: The sons' defense of their reading
steps.stepSummary: The sons of רבי חייא answer that 'from dovecote to dovecote' does not mean a dovecote ladder. It just means moving it among several dovecotes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the others (the sons), how would they answer? Does the ברייתא say 'a dovecote ladder'? It says 'from dovecote to dovecote,' and that means even to several dovecotes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the sons of רבי חייא would push back against the proof from the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons read the phrase as describing a route, not the type of ladder. The ladder can be an attic ladder, and the ברייתא just teaches that it may be carried from one dovecote to another, even to many. So the wording does not force the reading of Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other side? How do they answer?
Does it teach...? (a challenge to someone's reading)
Dovecotes (plural)

phrases.english: And the others (the sons), how do they answer?
Does it teach 'a dovecote ladder'?
It teaches 'from dovecote to dovecote'
and that means even to several dovecotes

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the proof from the wording in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the wording. It does not prove that the sons are right.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'משובך לשובך' describes where the ladder goes, not what kind of ladder it is.

steps.title: Second version: the sons permitted tilting an attic ladder
steps.stepSummary: In another version, the sons had permitted tilting an attic ladder, and רבי חייא told them to go back and forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the story went like this: the sons told him, 'A case of tilting an attic ladder came to us, and we permitted it.' He said to them, 'Go out and forbid what you permitted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version (איכא דאמרי) of the story of רבי חייא's sons. Here the question was about tilting, not carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version the sons permitted carrying a ladder. Here they permitted only tilting, which is a smaller action than carrying, but they allowed it even with an attic ladder. רבי חייא still forbade it. The next step explains why the sons made this mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: Tilting (leaning the ladder over rather than carrying it)
Go out and forbid

phrases.english: Some say: they said to him
the tilting of an attic ladder
came to our hands, and we permitted it
He said to them
Go out and forbid what you permitted

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the story told in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tilting an attic ladder is forbidden, even though the sons had permitted it.

steps.title: The sons' mistake about רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: The sons thought רבי דוסא was more lenient than the תנא קמא. Really he is more stringent.
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought: what the תנא קמא forbids (an attic ladder), רבי דוסא permits by tilting. But that is not so. What the תנא קמא permits (carrying a dovecote ladder), רבי דוסא forbids, allowing only tilting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the sons' error and corrects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons read רבי דוסא's 'tilting' as an extra leniency that adds the attic ladder. The גמרא says the opposite: רבי דוסא is talking only about a dovecote ladder. He limits how it may be moved, so tilting is allowed but carrying is not. So an attic ladder stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: They thought (introduces a mistaken assumption)
But it is not so
Permits
Forbids

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי דוסא adds a new kind of ladder. He takes the same dovecote ladder and limits HOW it may be moved: only by tilting.
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, an attic ladder may not be moved on יום טוב. רבי דוסא is stricter than the תנא קמא, not more lenient.

phrases.english: They thought:
what the first tanna forbids (an attic ladder)
Rabbi Dosa permits (by tilting)
But it is not so
what the first tanna permits (carrying a dovecote ladder)
Rabbi Dosa forbids (he allows only tilting)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי חייא forbade what the sons had permitted in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the sons' reading of רבי דוסא as more lenient than the תנא קמא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They read tilting as an extra leniency that adds the attic ladder. Really it limits how a dovecote ladder may be moved.

steps.title: On שמחת יום טוב, בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's 'but one may tilt it from window to window,' the גמרא notes a pattern: on שמחת יום טוב, בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'But one may tilt it from window to window,' and so on. So it seems that regarding the joy of יום טוב, בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and draws a general rule from it. This sets up the next move in the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית שמאי forbid carrying the ladder and allow only tilting, while בית הלל permit carrying, even though the ladder is used to get doves for the festive meal. So when שמחת יום טוב is at stake, בית שמאי take the strict side and בית הלל the lenient side. The גמרא will now work with this pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. (the quote from the משנה continues)
Apparently, it follows that
The joy of the festival (including the festive meal)
On the strict side
On the lenient side

phrases.english: The mishna said: But one may tilt it from window to window, etc.
Apparently,
regarding the joy of the festival
Beit Shammai are on the strict side
and Beit Hillel are on the lenient side

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of רבי חייא's sons and returns to the משנה to open a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Regarding שמחת יום טוב, בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient.
steps.whyThisMatters: This general pattern about how בית שמאי and בית הלל treat שמחת יום טוב is the starting point for the discussion that follows.

steps.title: A contradiction from the first משנה about covering blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about covering blood on יום טוב. There בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict, the opposite of the pattern just noted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא raises a contradiction: if someone slaughters a wild animal or a bird on יום טוב, בית שמאי say he may dig up earth with a shovel and cover the blood. בית הלל say he may not slaughter at all unless he had earth ready from before יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the pattern from Step 11. It quotes a משנה where בית שמאי are the lenient ones and בית הלל are the strict ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11 the rule was: on שמחת יום טוב, בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient. Here בית שמאי let a person dig fresh earth on יום טוב so he can slaughter and enjoy the meat. בית הלל do not allow it unless the earth was prepared in advance. That looks like the opposite pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (one source set against another)
A wild animal and a bird, whose blood must be covered (כיסוי הדם)
A shovel or digging tool
Earth that was prepared ahead of time
While it was still day, meaning before יום טוב began

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
One who slaughters a wild animal or a bird on Yom Tov,
Beit Shammai say:
He may dig with a shovel and cover [the blood],
and Beit Hillel say:
He may not slaughter unless

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה לוֹ עָפָר מוּכָן מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
phrases.english: he had earth prepared while it was still day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the pattern stated in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that on שמחת יום טוב בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה about covering blood, בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict. This is the reverse of the pattern.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the opinions are reversed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that in the covering-blood משנה, the names of בית שמאי and בית הלל should be switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the opinions are switched around.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the contradiction by saying the two opinions in the covering-blood משנה are attached to the wrong names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are switched, בית הלל become the lenient ones about digging and בית שמאי the strict ones. Then the pattern from Step 11 holds again. This is a strong answer, because it changes the text of a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The opinions are reversed (switch who said what)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The opinions are reversed.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the attribution of opinions in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The covering-blood משנה shows בית שמאי lenient and בית הלל strict
steps.terutzMaskana: Switch the names, and בית הלל are lenient there too

steps.title: Maybe בית שמאי are lenient only when a shovel is already in the ground
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needs to switch the names. Maybe בית שמאי allow digging only when a shovel is already stuck in the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know there is really a contradiction? Maybe בית שמאי only allow it there, when a shovel is already stuck in the ground. Where there is no shovel stuck in the ground, they would not allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן. It shows the contradiction can be solved without switching any names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a shovel is already stuck in the ground, digging is very easy, so בית שמאי can be lenient there. That is a special case. It does not mean בית שמאי are lenient about שמחת יום טוב in general, so they can still be strict about the ladder.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know?
Perhaps
They only said it up to here (their ruling is limited to this case)
A shovel that is already stuck in the ground

phrases.english: From where [do you know this]?
Perhaps they only said [their ruling]
Beit Shammai, there,
only where there is a shovel stuck in [the ground],

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דָּקָר נָעוּץ — לָא.
phrases.english: but where there is no shovel stuck in — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the need for רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects that the covering-blood משנה really contradicts the pattern, so switching names is not needed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בית שמאי's leniency may be limited to a case where a shovel is already in the ground

steps.title: Or maybe בית הלל are lenient only because the dovecote shows his intent
steps.stepSummary: A second way to avoid the contradiction: בית הלל are lenient with the ladder only because the dovecote makes it clear what he is doing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or also: maybe בית הלל only allow it here, with the ladder, because his dovecote shows what he is doing. There, with the digging, they would not allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second reason why switching names is not needed. This time it explains בית הלל's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the ladder, people can see that he is taking it to the dovecote, so nobody will think he is fixing his roof. That is why בית הלל can be lenient there. With digging earth there is no such sign, so בית הלל can be strict there without contradicting themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: Or also, alternatively
His dovecote proves about him (it shows his permitted purpose)

steps.whatToRemember: Each case has its own special factor: the shovel already in the ground, or the dovecote that shows his intent. So the covering-blood משנה does not truly contradict the pattern, and רבי יוחנן's answer must belong somewhere else.

phrases.english: Or alternatively:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית הִלֵּל הָכָא,
phrases.english: Beit Hillel only said [their ruling] here,
because his dovecote proves [his purpose] about him,
but there — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית הִלֵּל הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reason to reject the need for רבי יוחנן's answer
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the contradiction from בית הלל's side
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בית הלל's leniency with the ladder depends on the dovecote showing his intent, which does not apply to digging

steps.title: The real contradiction is the משנה about taking young doves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves רבי יוחנן's statement to a different contradiction. It quotes the משנה about taking young doves on יום טוב, where בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty: בית שמאי say a person may not take young doves on יום טוב unless he shook them before יום טוב. בית הלל say he may stand before יום טוב and say, 'I will take this one and that one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רבי יוחנן's answer was not about the covering-blood משנה. It now quotes the doves משנה, which sets up the real contradiction to be worked out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the doves משנה, בית שמאי require a physical action (shaking) to prepare the doves, and בית הלל accept just saying words. The point of difficulty is that the covering-blood משנה shows the opposite roles. בית שמאי there let a person dig with no preparation, while בית הלל require earth prepared in advance. This sharper contradiction is where רבי יוחנן's 'the opinions are reversed' really belongs.

keyTerms.meaning: If there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty
He shook (the doves, as a physical act of preparation)
This one and that one I will take (preparing by words alone)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is dropping רבי יוחנן. It keeps his answer, 'the opinions are reversed,' and just moves it to a different pair of sources, where the contradiction is stronger.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that בית הלל accept preparation by words (designating) where בית שמאי demand a physical act. That idea about הכנה for יום טוב runs through the rest of the sugya.

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difficulty,
this is the difficulty:
Beit Shammai say:
He may not take [young doves] unless
he shook [them] while it was still day,
and Beit Hillel say:
He stands and says,
'This one and that one I will take.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Steps 14 and 15 remove the first contradiction, this moves רבי יוחנן's answer to a new contradiction
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of בית שמאי and בית הלל between the covering-blood משנה and the doves משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the doves משנה, בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient about preparation. In the covering-blood משנה, the roles are reversed.

steps.title: The young doves show בית שמאי are strict even when holiday joy is at stake
steps.stepSummary: From the young-doves משנה, the גמרא learns that about שמחת יום טוב, בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient. It then sets this against the covering-blood משנה, which shows the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems that about the joy of יום טוב, בית שמאי are strict and בית הלל are lenient. But there is a contradiction from the משנה of 'one who slaughters a wild animal or a bird on יום טוב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the young-doves משנה and points out that it clashes with the covering-blood משנה. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the young doves, בית הלל allow a looser way of preparing the birds so a person can eat meat on יום טוב, while בית שמאי insist on stricter preparation the day before. In the covering-blood משנה, בית שמאי allow digging to cover the blood so the person can enjoy meat, while בית הלל forbid slaughtering unless dirt was ready. Each side looks inconsistent about how much weight it gives to שמחת יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: So it seems / evidently (draws a conclusion)
The מצוה of rejoicing on the festival
Strict / lenient
And they set them against each other (raises a contradiction)
A wild animal and a bird (their blood must be covered)

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same covering-blood contradiction from step 12, but it is now aimed at a different pair of sources. Here it is set against the young-doves משנה, not the ladder משנה.

phrases.english: Apparently, regarding the joy of the Festival,
Beit Shammai are stringent
and Beit Hillel are lenient.
And raise a contradiction:
One who slaughters a wild animal or a bird on a Festival
phrases.notes: There בית שמאי are lenient about digging to cover the blood, and בית הלל are strict.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא, גַּבֵּי שִׂמְחַת יוֹם טוֹב בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְחוּמְרָא וּבֵית הִלֵּל לְקוּלָּא, וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second version begun in step 16 by drawing the conclusion from the young-doves משנה and setting it against the covering-blood משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of בית שמאי and בית הלל about שמחת יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In one משנה, בית שמאי are strict even though holiday joy is at stake. In the other, they are lenient because of holiday joy. בית הלל flip the opposite way.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the names are switched
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רבי יוחנן said 'the opinions are switched' to answer this contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the opinions are switched.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן fixes the contradiction by saying that in the covering-blood משנה, the names of בית שמאי and בית הלל should be swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the swap, בית שמאי are strict about covering the blood, just as they are strict with the young doves. בית הלל become lenient in both places. Both sides now stay consistent about שמחת יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The opinions are switched (swap who said what)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The attribution of the opinions is reversed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: swapping the names in one משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The covering-blood משנה is read as written, with בית שמאי lenient.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read the covering-blood משנה with the names swapped, so each side matches its position on the young doves.

steps.title: Maybe בית שמאי were lenient only with a shovel already in the ground
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether the swap is needed. Perhaps בית שמאי's leniency about covering blood applies only when a shovel is already stuck in the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe that is not so: בית שמאי only said their lenient view where there is a shovel already stuck in the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's answer by offering another way to remove the contradiction without changing the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a shovel is already stuck in loose earth, digging involves very little work. So בית שמאי's leniency in that case would not show a general softness about שמחת יום טוב. They could still be strict with the young doves, and there would be no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps it is not so
They only said (their view) in this case
A shovel already stuck in the ground

phrases.english: But perhaps that is not so:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא אָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai only stated their view
where there is an embedded shovel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא לָא הִיא: עַד כָּאן לָא אָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבי יוחנן's swap in step 18 is necessary, using the same shovel idea from step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The need for רבי יוחנן's emendation, not the משניות themselves
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The contradiction can be solved by narrowing בית שמאי's leniency to an easy case, so there is no need to change the text.
